NO. 009 · Wetlands & Waterways / Ardeidae · Herons & Egrets

Little Egret

白鹭 · bái lù Egretta garzetta
Resident Abundant 55–65 cm Protected (China) IUCN LC

Black bill, black legs, yellow slippers — an egret that dresses with care

Snow-white, but with black legs and a pair of bright yellow slippers. In the breeding season two long white plumes trail from the nape and shaggy aigrettes hang over the breast, and it walks about as if dressed for a wedding. It is the bird you will meet at every patch of shallow water in the Delta.

Gallery

One scientific illustration for shape and colour blocks, two field photographs for how it looks in real light. Click any image to enlarge.

Identification

  • BillLong, thin and black — the key difference from Great Egret (yellow bill) and Intermediate Egret (yellow with a dark tip).
  • Legs & feetBlack legs with bright yellow toes — the famous 'black legs, yellow slippers' combination, identifiable at distance.
  • PlumesIn breeding condition two long white nape plumes and shaggy back and breast plumes appear, then are lost.
  • SizeMedium; neck slender; flies with the neck folded into an S and the legs trailing well beyond the tail.

Behaviour

Often stirs the shallows with one foot to startle small fish and shrimp before stabbing at them, but will also simply stand and wait. Solitary or in small groups; nests colonially in mangrove and bamboo with pond herons and night herons. Sensitive to water quality and human disturbance, which makes it a useful indicator of wetland health.

Voice

Quiet most of the time. A harsh 'kark' or 'krekk' when alarmed or squabbling, short and unpleasant; lower mutterings around the colony.

Where to find it in Zhuhai

  • Qi'ao Island mangroves
  • Hengqin Mangzhou Wetland
  • Lovers' Road seafront
  • Doumen fish ponds
Field note
Three white egrets, three answers — bill and legs do it: all-black bill with yellow feet is Little Egret; yellow bill with black legs is Great Egret; yellow bill with a dark tip, black legs and yellow feet is Intermediate Egret.
